nits.where: Prerequisites section: "the Doc Gen tools require an Enterprise Advanced license"
nits.problem: The Dossier ties the Enterprise Advanced license specifically to the docgen.readwrite scope (and says DocGen/Sign otherwise "depend on plan availability"), so stating the Doc Gen tools flatly require an Enterprise Advanced license slightly over-tightens a scope-level fact into a tool-level one.
nits.suggestion: Consider mirroring the Dossier's wording — attribute the Enterprise Advanced license to the Doc Gen scope (as the #plan-gated-tools and #enable-doc-gen sections already correctly do) rather than to the tools outright.

nits.where: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret step, line 115-116: "Copy the **Client ID** — a public identifier for this integration, a username for the connection rather than for any person — into..."
nits.problem: This glosses the OAuth term Client ID with a conceptual analogy, but the persona explicitly forbids teaching OAuth vocabulary ("client ID, client secret... Don't assume it — and don't teach it. They need the values in the right fields, not the concepts").
nits.suggestion: Drop the concept gloss and keep the action terse: "Copy the **Client ID** into the Speakeasy AI Control Plane's Client ID field." The reader only needs the value in the right field, not a definition.

nits.where: Provider setup intro, line 36-38: "The Box MCP Server signs users in with OAuth 2.0, a flow where each end user authorizes the connection with their own Box account."
nits.problem: Naming and glossing "OAuth 2.0" teaches OAuth vocabulary the persona says not to teach; the load-bearing fact (each user signs in with their own account) can stand without the OAuth framing.
nits.suggestion: Recast without the term: "When people connect from the Speakeasy AI Control Plane, each user signs in with their own Box account. To allow that, a Box admin creates one set of **Integration Credentials**..."

nits.where: Enable the Box AI API step, line 194: "Next to the **Box AI APIs** setting — it defines the developer users who can extend Box AI capabilities via the AI API — click **configure**." (same pattern at line 217, "Under **Box Doc Gen Permissions** — it defines who can create and manage Doc Gen templates — click **Configure**.")
nits.problem: These inline setting-definitions are explanation the work does not require — the reader only needs to locate the labeled setting and click Configure, not understand what the setting governs; the persona says "Terse beats taught. A console term appears as its verbatim bolded label, unexplained."
nits.suggestion: Remove the em-dash definitions: "Next to the **Box AI APIs** setting, click **configure**." and "Under **Box Doc Gen Permissions**, click **Configure**."

nits.where: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret step, line 117-118: "Copy the **Client Secret** — the connection's password, so store it like one — into..."
nits.problem: The gloss "the connection's password" teaches an OAuth concept the persona forbids, though the trailing "store it like one" is legitimate security guidance already covered by the step's opening warning to save it to a password manager.
nits.suggestion: Since the step already opens with "store the Client Secret in your password manager," trim the concept gloss: "Copy the **Client Secret** into the Speakeasy AI Control Plane's Client Secret field."

nits.problem: Each opening step packs navigation plus a tab-open into one numbered step ("go to the Box AI section, then open the Settings tab"; "go to Enterprise Settings, then open the Content and Sharing tab"), which the persona's one-action-per-step formatting rule discourages.
nits.suggestion: Split each into two numbered steps: one to open the section, a second to open the named tab (e.g. "1. Go to the **Box AI** section. 2. Open the **Settings** tab.").

nits.problem: Steps 4 ("To set a whole category at once...") and 5 ("To toggle individual tools instead...") are mutually-exclusive alternative paths, but they are numbered as sequential actions alongside step 6 (Save), implying the reader performs all three in order.
nits.suggestion: Present the category-level and per-tool paths as two labeled choices (prose or a bulleted either/or) rather than consecutive numbered steps, then keep the shared **Save** as the closing numbered action.

nits.where: setup.md#check-access-scopes — "In the Access scopes section of the credential entry, confirm the selected scopes cover the tool areas your users need."
nits.problem: The guide never tells the reader which scope is the baseline needed for the core content tools, nor whether any scope is pre-selected by default, so a reader unsure what their users need could save the entry with no scope (or the wrong one) selected and end up with a non-functional connection.
nits.suggestion: If the Dossier can establish it at capture time, state that the general content scope (root_readwrite / its console label) must be selected for the core file and search tools, and note the default-selected state of the Access scopes checkboxes; the Dossier currently flags the label-to-string mapping and default state as open questions, so this needs console verification when screenshots are captured.
